as: Assamese: Use modern Assamese punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
bn: Bengali: Use modern Bengali punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
gu: Gujarati: Use conventional modern Gujarati sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
hi: Hindi: Use modern Hindi punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
kn: Kannada: Use conventional modern Kannada sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
ml: Malayalam: Use conventional modern Malayalam sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
mr: Marathi: Use conventional modern Marathi sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
or: Odia: Use modern Odia punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
pa: Punjabi: Use modern Punjabi punctuation. Danda (।) may mark a natural sentence boundary but is not mandatory; use double danda (॥) only for genuine verse or sectional text.
ta: Tamil: Use conventional modern Tamil sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
te: Telugu: Use conventional modern Telugu sentence and clause punctuation only where the wording supports it.
ur: Urdu: Prefer Urdu comma (،), semicolon (؛), question mark (؟), and full stop (۔) where natural. Preserve logical Unicode order and never reverse or reshape text; a Western mark may remain appropriate inside a clearly code-switched span.
